label: GO after a reward, when S2 was just rewarded or the agent is choosing a2 (early-episode)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew=1 at D1), and almost only when the evidence/choice favours a2/S2: the rewarded state was S2 or the agent is about to pick a2 (model_act==2, its own computed choice; 89% of mass). Without the time clause this has 99% recall but 0.41 precision: activity fades over the episode (rate ~10% of steps in trials 0-39, <2% after 50, ~0 by 90), which the model value (active only for value in [7.73, 8.10)) proxies equally well (dev F1 0.84 with a value band instead of ep_trial). Largest activations (near max) are a2 choices right after a rewarded trial that reached S2 (often a rare-rewarded a1 trial followed by a model-based switch to a2); repeated a2 after common S2 rewards give mid-size activations. Never fires after unrewarded trials, at D1/D2, or on most a1 choices after S1 rewards. No future variables used.

issues: The label's second branch, 'or the agent is about to pick a2', is wrong. When S1 was just rewarded and the agent picks a2, the unit never fires: (phase==GO)&(prev_reward==1)&(model_act==2)&(prev_state==1)&(ep_trial<45) has precision 0.00 over 4816 predicted steps (dev). Rewarded-S1 trials never activate it, whichever way the agent chooses.

model_act==2 only appears to matter because of a window-edge artifact. At rel -3 the window has no previous trial, so prev_state is -1 and the S2 branch cannot fire; there model_act==2 stands in for 'S2 was rewarded' (precision 0.86). Those rel -3 steps carry 18% of activations. On trials with a known prev_state, the unit follows prev_state==2 regardless of the upcoming choice: S2 rewarded then a1 has precision 0.93, S2 rewarded then a2 has precision 0.89.

So the claim that model_act==2 'holds 89% of the activation mass' is a correlation, not the explanation. The unit is simply 'GO after S2 was rewarded'. a2 choices dominate the mass because agents mostly repeat a2 after an S2 reward.

The other claims check out on dev. Activity is GO-only (D1 and D2 have zero active steps). There is zero activation after unrewarded trials. The time fade is real: the base predicate restricted to ep_trial>=45 has precision 0.12 and recall 0.17, and the value band works as well as ep_trial (F1 0.839 dev). The magnitude claim holds: rare-rewarded a1 followed by a switch to a2 has mass_recall/recall about 2.2x, and repeated common-S2 a2 choices are about average.
The remaining misses (about 18%) are mostly the episode-late tail at ep_trial>=45, which is low-precision. That is the stated fade, not a new class.
skeptic.revised_label: GO after S2 was just rewarded (whichever action is chosen next), early in the episode; at the window's first trial, where prev_state is unknown, the a2 choice stands in for it
